topic: Longitudinal comparison, registration and PET in head & neck imaging (Margin / hnrad)

findings.title: itk-elastix (ITKElastix): ITK Python interface to elastix
findings.summary: Python wrapping of the elastix toolbox: rigid, affine and B-spline deformable registration with ready-made parameter-map presets. Binary wheels for Windows/macOS/Linux, pip installable, multi-threaded CPU cost-function derivative computation. No GPU required.
findings.relevance: Primary registration engine for Margin's prior-vs-current CT/MR alignment: rigid first pass on the neck, then B-spline for post-surgical deformation.
findings.feasibility: VERIFIED on PyPI: itk-elastix 0.25.4 (Aug 2026) ships itk_elastix-0.25.4-cp311-abi3-win_amd64.whl. The abi3 stable-ABI wheel installs on Python 3.11 and every later CPython, so Python 3.13 on Windows works with a plain user-level `pip install itk-elastix` - no compiler, no admin, no CUDA.

findings.title: itk-elastix: Medical image registration in Python (SciPy 2023)
findings.summary: Reference paper for itk-elastix: parameter-object API, preset parameter maps (rigid/affine/bspline), multi-resolution pyramid workflow, CPU parallelisation of the cost-function derivative, and persistence of transform parameter maps.
findings.relevance: Design template for Margin's registration service; stored parameter maps make each comparison reproducible and auditable.
findings.feasibility: Documentation only; described API is CPU-only.

findings.title: SimpleITK-Elastix / SimpleITK-SimpleElastix unofficial PyPI wheels
findings.summary: SimpleElastix is not distributed by the official SimpleITK PyPI package because of a naming conflict; elastix-enabled SimpleITK is published only as unofficial third-party wheels (win_amd64, manylinux, macOS) maintained outside the Insight Software Consortium.
findings.relevance: Important negative result: do NOT plan Margin around sitk.ElastixImageFilter. Use itk-elastix for registration and keep stock SimpleITK for I/O, resampling and metrics.
findings.feasibility: Unofficial wheels lag Python releases and are a provenance/supply-chain concern for a clinical tool on a corporate machine. Prefer itk-elastix.

findings.title: ANTsPy - Advanced Normalization Tools in Python (SyN registration)
findings.summary: Mature registration/segmentation library exposing ants.registration with Rigid, Affine, SyN and SyNCC transforms plus ants.apply_transforms for propagating labels across timepoints. SyN is the reference-standard deformable method in most benchmark comparisons.
findings.relevance: Alternative deformable backend; apply_transforms is the cleanest way to carry a prior-study tumour contour or nodal ROI onto the current study for side-by-side measurement.
findings.feasibility: pip binary wheels; Windows needs the MSVC redistributable (normally already present on a managed image). CPU-only. SyN on a full neck CT can take minutes on CPU - run as an async FastAPI background job. Verify Python 3.13 wheel availability.

findings.title: uniGradICON: a foundation model for medical image registration
findings.summary: Single pretrained deep registration network with zero-shot generalisation across anatomies and modalities, plus optional instance-optimisation refinement. Competitive Dice against task-specific networks without retraining; code and weights released.
findings.relevance: Candidate one-shot deformable alignment for Margin with no local training data; could produce a fast initial warp that elastix then refines.
findings.feasibility: PyTorch CPU wheels are pip-installable at user level; a 3D forward pass plus instance optimisation on an Intel iGPU box is slow (tens of seconds to minutes) and memory-hungry. Benchmark before adopting.

findings.title: TransMorph: Transformer for unsupervised medical image registration
findings.summary: Swin-Transformer registration network that outperforms VoxelMorph-class CNNs on standard benchmarks; diffeomorphic and Bayesian variants with pretrained weights and full PyTorch training code.
findings.relevance: Reference architecture only - pretrained weights are brain-centric, so head & neck transfer is unproven and there is no neck training set available on a local-only device.
findings.feasibility: CPU inference possible but heavy for 3D transformer volumes. Not a near-term fit for Margin.

findings.title: VoxelMorph: unsupervised learning model for deformable registration
findings.summary: The original learning-based deformable registration framework: a CNN predicts a dense displacement field in one forward pass, orders of magnitude faster than iterative optimisation at comparable Dice on brain MRI.
findings.relevance: Baseline for judging whether a learned warp is worth the dependency cost in Margin versus iterative elastix.
findings.feasibility: TF/PyTorch; CPU inference feasible for modest volumes. Pretrained models are brain-only - not usable for neck out of the box.

findings.title: Multimodality image registration in the head-and-neck using a deep-learning-derived synthetic CT as a bridge
findings.summary: Phantom study imposing a neck-flexion deformation of up to 8 mm; synthetic-CT-bridged deformable registration remained valuable even under large neck flexion, with improvements on the order of the ~3 mm margins used clinically in head & neck radiotherapy.
findings.relevance: Direct evidence for Margin's core neck problem - flexion/extension differences between a current study and its prior. Justifies a two-stage pipeline (bone-weighted rigid init, then constrained B-spline) and sets a realistic few-millimetre accuracy expectation.
findings.feasibility: N/A - methodology guidance, no dependency.

findings.title: Comprehensive evaluation of ten deformable image registration algorithms for contour propagation between CT and CBCT in adaptive head & neck radiotherapy
findings.summary: Head-to-head comparison of ten DIR algorithms for neck contour propagation. DIR performed markedly better on bony structures than on soft-tissue organs; optical-flow methods ranked best and demons-based methods usually ranked last. Auto-propagated contours required review before clinical acceptance.
findings.relevance: Tells Margin to prefer bone-driven rigid alignment as the link between studies, to show any propagated contour as an editable suggestion rather than a measurement, and to avoid demons-family algorithms.
findings.feasibility: N/A

findings.title: Impact of robustness of deformable image registration on contour propagation and dose accumulation for head and neck adaptive radiotherapy
findings.venue_or_repo: PMC / J Appl Clin Med Phys
findings.summary: Quantifies how much DIR output varies with algorithm and parameter choice in the neck and how that variability propagates into contour and dose-accumulation error, showing DIR uncertainty is comparable to interobserver contouring variation.
findings.relevance: Supports surfacing a per-case registration-quality indicator in Margin (post-registration mutual information plus a Jacobian-determinant sanity check) rather than silently trusting the warp.
findings.feasibility: N/A

findings.title: NI-RADS in posttreatment head and neck cancer surveillance: a framework for standardized imaging with clinical impact
findings.summary: Review of the ACR NI-RADS lexicon: category 1-4 risk stratification reported separately for primary site and neck, a standardized lexicon of post-treatment findings, linked management recommendations, and the new MRI-specific NI-RADS 2025 version with modality-specific descriptors.
findings.relevance: Defines the structured-report schema Margin should emit: independent primary-site and neck categories, each with its own management action, with a CT/MRI descriptor split.
findings.feasibility: N/A - encode the lexicon as a local JSON file; no network, no model, no licensing cost.

findings.title: Diagnostic performance of the NI-RADS system for detecting recurrence in head and neck SCC (monocentric pilot)
findings.summary: Recurrence confirmed at 36% of primary sites and 27% of neck sites; NI-RADS category 1 showed 0% recurrence and category 4 showed 100% recurrence at both primary and neck sites, supporting the category-to-risk mapping.
findings.relevance: Posterior-risk numbers to display next to any Margin-suggested NI-RADS category so the surgeon sees a calibrated probability rather than a bare label.
findings.feasibility: N/A

findings.title: Early post-operative NI-RADS predicts recurrence and survival in high-risk oral cavity SCC undergoing adjuvant radiotherapy
findings.summary: Applies NI-RADS to imaging performed within 12 weeks of surgery in high-risk oral cavity SCC and shows prognostic value for recurrence and survival, i.e. the lexicon carries signal even on the difficult early post-surgical baseline study.
findings.relevance: Supports a Margin workflow that scores the first post-op baseline, not only the 3-month surveillance scan - directly relevant to a surgeon following their own post-op patients.
findings.feasibility: N/A

findings.title: Enhancing prediction of primary site recurrence in head and neck cancer using radiomics and uncertainty estimation
findings.summary: Machine-learning models on radiomic plus clinical features from pre- and post-treatment PET/CT in 249 patients reached mean AUC 0.820 for HNSCC recurrence, while a vision-transformer comparator reached only AUC 0.658. Adds explicit uncertainty estimation so low-confidence cases are flagged.
findings.relevance: Blueprint for Margin's recurrence-vs-post-treatment-change assist: classical radiomics on CPU outperforms the transformer here, and the uncertainty head is exactly the abstain behaviour a local clinical assistant needs.
findings.feasibility: Radiomic extraction plus a small scikit-learn model is trivially CPU-feasible and pip-installable. The published models are not distributed, so Margin should ship the feature panel and literature context, not a prediction, until locally validated.

findings.title: Deep learning based recurrence prediction in head and neck cancers after radiotherapy (3D PET/CT/dose model)
findings.venue_or_repo: Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Phys
findings.summary: 3D deep-learning model on FDG-PET/CT plus dose data from 157 patients gave averaged AUC 0.856 for locoregional recurrence; adding clinical factors raised average AUC to 0.892 with a best fold of 0.974.
findings.relevance: Upper bound on what recurrence prediction can achieve, and a caution: it needs RT dose maps and a training cohort, neither of which Margin has locally. Context, not something to reimplement.
findings.feasibility: No public weights; small single-centre cohort. Not implementable offline.

findings.title: PyRadiomics - IBSI-aligned radiomic feature extraction for PET/CT
findings.summary: Open-source Python package extracting IBSI-compliant first-order, shape and texture features from an image plus mask pair. On an SUV-scaled PET volume, first-order maximum gives SUVmax, mask volume gives MTV, and mean SUV times volume gives TLG. This study assessed inter-observer reproducibility of those features in FDG PET/CT.
findings.relevance: Single dependency that gives Margin SUVmax / SUVmean / MTV / TLG plus a texture panel for the recurrence-versus-inflammation question, straight from a SimpleITK image and mask.
findings.feasibility: BLOCKER (verified via PyPI JSON API): latest release is 3.1.0, uploaded 18 May 2023, and the newest Windows wheel is cp38-win_amd64 - no cp312 or cp313 wheels at all. On Python 3.13 with no admin rights and no MSVC build chain, `pip install pyradiomics` will fail. Either implement SUVmax/MTV/TLG directly with numpy+SimpleITK (they are simple reductions over a mask) or find a maintained fork before depending on it.

findings.title: QIICR Slicer PET DICOM SUV plugin - reference Python SUV factor implementation
findings.summary: Readable Python implementation of DICOM-header-driven SUV conversion: decay correction from RadiopharmaceuticalStartTime and half-life, Units handling (BQML vs CNTS vs PROPCPS), and SUVbw = activity concentration / (injected dose / body weight). The companion CLI also computes SUVlbm, SUVbsa and SUVibw.
findings.relevance: Exact formulas and header edge cases Margin's pydicom-based SUV scaler must reproduce; the multi-vendor decay-time and units quirks are what silently break home-grown SUV code.
findings.feasibility: Pure Python logic to port on top of pydicom - no new dependency, no GPU. Highest-value copy-the-logic finding for PET support.

findings.title: QIICR Slicer-SUVFactorCalculator (SUVbw, SUVlbm, SUVbsa, SUVibw from DICOM)
findings.summary: 3D Slicer CLI module that takes a PET DICOM series and computes the four standard SUV conversion factors. Serves as an independent, citable cross-check for any SUV scaling implementation.
findings.relevance: Validation oracle: run one anonymised PET series through it and compare against Margin's pydicom SUV output before trusting the number clinically.
findings.feasibility: C++ CLI inside Slicer so not embeddable, but Slicer itself installs per-user on Windows without admin. Use offline for validation only.

findings.title: LIFEx - PET/CT texture and MTV/TLG analysis software
findings.summary: Free desktop application for PET/CT quantification: SUVmax, MTV via 41%-of-SUVmax thresholding of automatically detected hypermetabolic regions, TLG, and a large texture panel. Widely cited as the reference implementation of the 41% threshold MTV protocol.
findings.relevance: Defines the MTV segmentation convention Margin should implement (selectable 41%-of-SUVmax and fixed SUV 2.5 modes) and gives a cross-check target for validating our numbers.
findings.license: free for research use, NOT open source; Java desktop app, no pip package
findings.feasibility: Not embeddable in Margin - Java binary and restrictive licence. Use only as an offline validation reference.

findings.title: Cornerstone3D VolumeViewport - per-volume colormap and opacity for PET/CT fusion
findings.summary: A VolumeViewport can hold multiple volume actors. setProperties applies to the first volume in a fusion, while setColormap and setOpacity take a volumeId, so CT stays greyscale while the PET actor gets a hot-metal colormap and adjustable alpha; colormap range maps to the current VOI range.
findings.relevance: The concrete API for Margin's PET/CT fusion viewport: one CT volume plus one resampled PET volume in the same viewport, with a fusion-opacity slider and SUV-unit VOI.
findings.feasibility: Browser/WebGL with Node 20 build; no Python or GPU-compute concern. Requires PET resampled onto the CT frame of reference, which the FastAPI/SimpleITK side should do server-side.

findings.title: OHIF Viewer v3.7 release notes - PET SUV units and window-level/colormap controls
findings.summary: OHIF 3.7 adopted Cornerstone3D modality units including petSeriesModule, so measurement statistics report SUV rather than raw counts, and added a WindowLevel component with histogram plus colormap and transparency control - the building blocks of a fusion UI.
findings.relevance: Prior art to copy rather than reinvent: Margin can mirror OHIF's SUV unit plumbing and fusion controls without adopting the whole OHIF shell.
findings.feasibility: Front-end only; the MIT licence allows lifting patterns or individual packages into Margin's React app.

findings.title: Results from the autoPET challenge on fully automated lesion segmentation in oncologic PET/CT
findings.summary: Benchmark over 1,014 FDG and 597 PSMA PET/CT studies; 27 submitted algorithms, overwhelmingly 3D nnU-Net with PET and CT concatenated as input channels. A plain nnU-Net baseline aligned well with manual lesion segmentation and near-top teams differed from it mainly by training tricks.
findings.relevance: If Margin ever auto-segments FDG-avid neck lesions to compute MTV/TLG, nnU-Net with PET+CT channels is the evidence-backed baseline - and the paper shows the elaborate variants buy little.
findings.license: nnU-Net is Apache-2.0; challenge data CC-BY-NC (verify per set)
findings.feasibility: nnU-Net CPU inference on a whole-body PET/CT is many minutes on an iGPU laptop, and the lesion models are whole-body rather than neck-specific. Future work behind an explicit run-analysis button, never on study open.

findings.title: Volumetric PET/CT parameters predict local response of HNSCC to chemoradiotherapy
findings.summary: MTV and TLG of the primary tumour predicted local response to chemoradiotherapy in head and neck SCC, outperforming SUVmax alone as prognostic markers.
findings.relevance: Evidence that Margin should track MTV and TLG over time, not just SUVmax - justifies the extra segmentation work in the PET panel.
findings.feasibility: N/A

findings.title: Multi-modality imaging parameters that predict rapid tumour regression in head and neck radiotherapy
findings.summary: Serial intra-treatment MRI/PET volumetry in head & neck cancer; adding week-1 and week-2 volume measurements improved prediction of later tumour volume (MAE 12.5% then 10.7%), and personalised per-patient models beat a generic population model.
findings.relevance: Quantitative backing for Margin's volume-trend chart: two early longitudinal points already carry predictive signal, so a per-patient volume trajectory is clinically meaningful rather than decorative.
findings.feasibility: N/A - informs a trend model that is a few lines of numpy.

findings.title: Tumour volume as a predictive parameter in sequential therapy of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma
findings.summary: In induction-chemotherapy HNSCC, the change in tumour volume between baseline and post-treatment imaging significantly affected overall survival (p = 0.026) and disease-free survival (p = 0.028).
findings.relevance: Outcome-level justification for making percent volume change a first-class number in Margin's longitudinal comparison view, alongside RECIST-style longest diameter.
findings.feasibility: N/A

findings.title: Approximation of head and neck cancer volumes in contrast-enhanced CT
findings.summary: Compares slice-by-slice manual volumetry against ellipsoid and other approximation formulas for head & neck tumour volume on contrast-enhanced CT, quantifying the error of the fast approximations clinicians actually use.
findings.relevance: Lets Margin offer a fast three-diameter ellipsoid volume estimate next to a full segmentation volume, with a published error bar so the surgeon knows which number to trust.
findings.feasibility: N/A - the ellipsoid formula is arithmetic on three caliper measurements already captured in the viewer.

findings.title: 18F-FDG-PET/CT for occult primary search in head & neck SCC of unknown primary: systematic review and meta-analysis
findings.summary: Pooled detection rate of the occult primary was 40% (95% CI 31-49%) across 16 studies and 724 patients when PET/CT follows a negative conventional work-up. Base of tongue, palatine tonsil and hypopharynx dominate the sites found.
findings.relevance: Sets the prior for Margin's unknown-primary hotspot map: a targeted anatomic checklist (both tonsils, both tongue-base halves, pyriform sinuses, nasopharynx) with the ~40% expected yield shown so the tool does not overpromise.
findings.feasibility: N/A - implement as a deterministic anatomic checklist keyed to a neck-region atlas; no model, no GPU.

findings.title: FDG-PET site-specific accuracy and false-positive rates in the unknown-primary neck (meta-analysis)
findings.venue_or_repo: Egyptian Journal of Radiology and Nuclear Medicine
findings.summary: Overall FDG-PET sensitivity 88.3%, specificity 74.9%, accuracy 78.8% for occult primary detection. False-positive rate was 39.3% in the tonsils versus 21.4% at the tongue base and 8.3% in the hypopharynx; sensitivity at the tongue base was 81.5%.
findings.relevance: Lets Margin annotate each unknown-primary hotspot with a site-specific false-positive prior - a tonsillar hotspot is much weaker evidence than a hypopharyngeal one, exactly the nuance a surgeon wants before directed biopsy or lingual tonsillectomy.
findings.feasibility: N/A - a small static lookup table in the app.

findings.title: PET-CT test properties for HPV-positive unknown primary of the neck (FIND trial correlative study)
findings.summary: Prospective-trial correlative analysis of PET/CT test characteristics specifically in HPV-positive carcinoma of unknown primary of the neck - the exact population in which transoral robotic and lingual tonsillectomy decisions are made.
findings.relevance: Most current, most HPV-relevant evidence to cite in Margin's unknown-primary panel; refreshes older meta-analytic priors for today's oropharyngeal case mix.
findings.feasibility: N/A - abstract only reviewed; obtain full text before hard-coding a numeric prior.

gaps: No head-&-neck-specific pretrained deep registration weights exist publicly - uniGradICON / TransMorph / VoxelMorph checkpoints are brain- or thorax-centric, so any learned warp in the neck is off-distribution and unvalidated.

Python 3.13 wheels: itk-elastix is CONFIRMED fine (cp311-abi3 win_amd64 covers 3.13); pyradiomics is CONFIRMED broken (3.1.0, May 2023, newest Windows wheel is cp38). antspyx was NOT verified - check before depending on it. Whether a maintained pyradiomics fork with modern wheels exists is unresolved.

No published benchmark of CPU-only registration wall-clock time for a full neck CT pair on an Intel iGPU class machine - Margin must measure locally; a downsampled 2 mm rigid pass is likely the only interactive-latency option.

No open-source validated tool automates NI-RADS category assignment from images; all published work is human-read scoring. Margin can provide structured data entry plus the lexicon, not an automated category.

No head & neck specific validation of registering post-surgical free-flap reconstruction, which is exactly where deformable registration and radiomic features are most likely to fail; flap anatomy is essentially absent from public training sets.

No maintained pip-installable PET SUV library was found - the QIICR code is the reference implementation but must be ported; budget real effort for DICOM units and decay-correction edge cases across scanner vendors.
Evidence linking longitudinal volume change to outcome comes mostly from radiotherapy cohorts; post-surgical surveillance volumetry evidence is thinner.
Cornerstone3D documentation covers the fusion API but no canonical end-to-end PET/CT fusion example with SUV window presets was located - expect nontrivial front-end work.
